Earlier scenes:
(none)

This scene:
在古代，很多医生不知道怎么用药。所以他们找到了很多植物对药。神农先看到很多病人，他们吃很多植物对药。但是我觉得他们的吃的植物，让他们病人。神农觉得这个植物可能特别是毒。所以他想找一个植物对药，他们可以吃对药。正好，他找到了一把花，他想把花放在茶里，对药。

The teacher's corrections on this scene (student words：her correction, her note):
- 所以他们找到了很多植物对药：来做药
- 神农先看到很多病人，他们吃很多植物对药：better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears；吃了很多植物，了completed
- 但是我觉得他们的吃的植物，让他们病人：他们吃的植物让他们生病，让Sb. + V./Adj.
- 神农觉得这个植物可能特别是毒：可能毒性特别强，”特别是+N, + Clause” is used to single out a typical example
- 所以他想找一个植物对药，他们可以吃对药：找一个可以做药的植物；这样，他们可以……
- 他想把花放在茶里，对药：做成药

The system's feedback items:
1. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 植物对药：很多可以做药的植物，The phrase “对药” is not a valid verb-object expression here; “做药” means that the plants can be made into medicine. [rule: word_choice]
2. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 对药：来治病，“对药” cannot describe the purpose of eating plants; “来治病” clearly expresses that the patients eat them in order to treat an illness. [rule: word_choice]
3. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 他们的吃的植物，让他们病人：他们吃的植物让他们生病，Use a verb phrase after “让”; “病人” is a noun meaning a sick person, while “生病” is the verb phrase for becoming ill. [rule: word_class_misuse]
4. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 特别是毒：特别有毒，“是毒” is not the correct predicate for a poisonous plant; “有毒” describes the plant as poisonous, and it can follow “特别”. [vocab list]
5. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 一个植物对药：一种可以做药的植物，“对药” is not a suitable expression, and the modifier needs to come before “植物” with “的”; “一种” is also the natural measure word for a type of plant. [rule: attributive_modifier_de]
6. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 吃对药：吃，“对药” cannot follow “吃”; after the plant has been described as medicine, “人们可以吃” is complete. [rule: word_choice]
7. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 对药：做药，“对药” is not a valid expression for making medicine; “做药” states the intended use of the flowers. [rule: word_choice]
8. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 神农先看到很多病人：一个叫神农的人先看到了很多病人，This is the first mention of this character, so introduce him with a full noun phrase rather than using only his name. [rule: character_introduction_first_mention]
9. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 这个植物：有些植物，No particular single plant has been introduced before this point, so “这个植物” has no clear referent; use a noun phrase that matches the previously mentioned plants. [rule: ambiguous_reference]
10. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 他们可以吃：人们可以吃，Several groups have appeared earlier, including doctors and patients, so “他们” is ambiguous here; “人们” clearly identifies the intended group. [rule: ambiguous_reference]
11. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 他想把花放在茶里：他想把它放在茶里，“一把花” was mentioned immediately before, with no competing object, so a pronoun is more natural for this close re-occurrence. [rule: redundancy_delete]
12. [Coherence: temporality, error] Coherence (Temporality): 先看到：先看到了，This is a completed event in the past narrative, so add “了” after the resultative complement “到”. [rule: aspect_le_completed]
13. [Coherence: temporality, error] Coherence (Temporality): 吃很多植物：吃了很多植物，The patients’ eating is presented as a completed past action, so it needs “了”. [rule: aspect_le_completed]

items.reason: “对药” is not a valid expression here, while “可以做药的植物” is correct.
“吃植物对药” is not valid, and “来治病” correctly states the purpose.
“让” needs a verb or adjective result, so “让他们生病” is correct.
“特别是毒” is not a suitable predicate here, whereas “特别有毒” is grammatical and natural.
“一个植物对药” has both an invalid expression and an incorrectly formed modifier, and the replacement is correct.
“对药” cannot follow “吃,” and the object can be omitted in this context.
“对药” is invalid here, and “做药” is a grammatical way to express making medicine.
神农 is first introduced here, and the correction also correctly marks the completed event with “了.”
No particular plant has been established as the referent of “这个植物,” while “有些植物” fits the earlier mention.
The teacher accepts “他们” here as referring to the previously mentioned patients, so this is not a required correction.
Repeating “花” immediately after its introduction is acceptable and not a reference error.
This past completed seeing event needs “了” after the resultative complement “到.”
The patients’ eating is a completed story event, so “吃了很多植物” is required.
